column2: Try to go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, even on weekends. Keep your room dark, cool and quiet, and put screens away for half an hour before bed. Avoid caffeine in the afternoon.

Take a few slow, deep breaths, in through your nose and out through your mouth. Write down what is bothering you and pick one small step you can take today. A short walk and talking to someone you trust can help too.

Study in short sessions of about 25 minutes with short breaks in between. Test yourself instead of just rereading, and explain the ideas out loud as if you were teaching someone. Start a few days early instead of cramming the night before.
Put your phone in another room and work on one task at a time. Set a timer for 25 minutes and focus only on that task until it rings, then take a short break.
Break the job into a tiny first step that takes less than five minutes, and start that step right now. Once you begin, it is much easier to keep going. Reward yourself when you finish.
Join a club, class or team around something you enjoy, so you see the same people regularly. Ask questions and listen to the answers, and don't be afraid to suggest doing something together.
Start small with something you enjoy, like a brisk 20-minute walk most days. Add a little more each week, mix in some strength exercises, and remember that consistency matters more than intensity.
Fill half your plate with vegetables and fruit, choose whole grains, and drink water instead of sugary drinks. Cooking simple meals at home makes it easier to eat well.
Keep a water bottle with you and sip through the day. A good sign you are drinking enough is that you rarely feel thirsty.
Practice out loud several times, ideally in front of a friend. Know your opening lines by heart, speak a little slower than feels natural, and remember that the audience wants you to do well.
Write down what you spend for a month to see where your money goes. Then set aside a fixed amount as soon as you get paid, before you spend on anything else.
Make a short list each morning of the three most important things to do that day, and do the hardest one first. Say no to things that don't fit your priorities.
Research the company, practice answers to common questions out loud, and prepare two or three questions of your own. Arrive a little early and give specific examples of things you have done.
Drink a glass of water, rest in a quiet, dark room and step away from screens for a while. If headaches are severe, sudden or keep coming back, see a doctor.
Rest, drink plenty of fluids and wash your hands often so you don't pass it on. If you have trouble breathing or a high fever that won't go down, see a doctor.
Practice a little every day rather than a lot once a week. Learn the most common words first, listen to the language in songs and shows, and try speaking even when you make mistakes.
Carry a book with you and read a few pages whenever you are waiting. Pick books you actually enjoy, and it's fine to stop one that doesn't grab you.

Get outside in daylight, move your body, and spend time with people you like. Writing down three good things each evening can shift your mood over time. If sadness lasts for weeks, talk to someone you trust or a professional.
Wait until you are both calm, then listen fully before you answer. Talk about how you feel instead of blaming, and look for a solution you can both accept.

Do small things that stretch you a little every day, like saying hello to someone new. Keep a list of things you have done well, and remember that most people are thinking about themselves, not judging you.
Attach the new habit to something you already do every day, like flossing right after brushing. Make it so small you can't fail, and track it on a calendar.
Turn off notifications you don't need, keep your phone out of the bedroom, and set specific times to check messages instead of checking constantly.
Most houseplants die from too much water, not too little. Check that the top of the soil is dry before watering, give them as much light as they like, and use pots with drainage holes.
Start with a few simple recipes and make them several times until they feel easy. Taste as you go, use a sharp knife, and get everything chopped before you turn on the heat.
Give your pet a regular routine for meals, walks and play, and reward good behavior right away. Regular vet checkups help keep them healthy.
Make a packing list a few days before, roll your clothes to save space, and keep important documents and medicine in your carry-on bag.
Get enough sleep, because sleep locks in memories. Review new things a day later and again a week later, and connect new facts to things you already know.
Write a messy first draft quickly without stopping to fix it, then go back and edit. Read it out loud to catch awkward sentences, and cut words that don't add anything.
